title: Tidy Tools for Chinese, Japanese and Korean Text
text: Text tooling R assumes words separated whitespace, Chinese, Japanese Korean writing oblige. tidytext splits whitespace. Chinese Japanese don’t use whitespace. Give tidytext English sentence get words; give 我今天很開心 get either one undifferentiated blob six isolated characters. Neither right — 開心 (“happy”) one word two characters, splitting destroys signal trying measure. tidycjk tells script language text column , much CJK, characters contains, wide print, normalises width variants away — tidy verbs return tibbles.

title: Tidy Tools for Chinese, Japanese and Korean Text
text: Two verbs take (data, column) return tibble, drop dplyr pipeline. prop_with_cjk answers “many rows CJK ”; mean_ratio answers “CJK ”. corpus English one stray ideograph per row scores high first near zero second.
code: library(tidycjk)  posts <- data.frame(   id = 1:5,   text = c(     "我今天很開心",           # Chinese     "こんにちは、元気ですか",   # Japanese, with kana     "안녕하세요",              # Korean     "東京都",                 # Japanese written without kana     "no CJK here at all"   ) )  cjk_summary(posts, text) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   n_docs n_with_cjk prop_with_cjk mean_ratio #>    <int>      <int>         <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1      5          4           0.8        0.8 cjk_char_counts(posts, text) #> # A tibble: 25 × 5 #>    char  codepoint script   block                      n #>    <chr>     <int> <chr>    <chr>                  <int> #>  1 我        25105 han      CJK Unified Ideographs     1 #>  2 今        20170 han      CJK Unified Ideographs     1 #>  3 天        22825 han      CJK Unified Ideographs     1 #>  4 很        24456 han      CJK Unified Ideographs     1 #>  5 開        38283 han      CJK Unified Ideographs     1 #>  6 心        24515 han      CJK Unified Ideographs     1 #>  7 こ        12371 hiragana Hiragana                   1 #>  8 ん        12435 hiragana Hiragana                   1 #>  9 に        12395 hiragana Hiragana                   1 #> 10 ち        12385 hiragana Hiragana                   1 #> # ℹ 15 more rows

title: Tidy Tools for Chinese, Japanese and Korean Text
text: cjk_tokens() CJK-aware counterpart tidytext’s unnest_tokens(). word ends fact language rather Unicode, segmenter bundled engine required — quietly handing back character tokens someone asked words mistake package exists avoid. "character" one engine needs dictionary: one token per CJK character, non-CJK runs split whitespace. character tokenisation, word segmentation. real Chinese word segmentation, register jiebaR. archived CRAN 2025-05-01, install remotes::install_github("qinwf/jiebaR"), : shape works segmenter can call R.
code: cjk_tokens(posts[1:2, ], text, engine = "character") #> # A tibble: 17 × 3 #>       id text         token #>    <int> <chr>        <chr> #>  1     1 我今天很開心 我 #>  2     1 我今天很開心 今 #>  3     1 我今天很開心 天 #>  4     1 我今天很開心 很 #>  5     1 我今天很開心 開 #>  6     1 我今天很開心 心 #>  7     2 こんにちは、元気ですか こ #>  8     2 こんにちは、元気ですか ん #>  9     2 こんにちは、元気ですか に #> 10     2 こんにちは、元気ですか ち #> # ℹ 7 more rows cjk_segment("hello 中文 world", engine = "character") #> [[1]] #> [1] "hello" "中"    "文"    "world" register_cjk_segmenter("jiebar", function(x, ...) {   worker <- jiebaR::worker(...)   lapply(x, function(s) {     if (is.na(s)) return(NA_character_)     if (!nzchar(s)) return(character(0))     as.character(jiebaR::segment(s, worker))   }) })  cjk_segment("我今天很開心", engine = "jiebar")

title: Tidy Tools for Chinese, Japanese and Korean Text
text: nchar() counts characters. terminal counts columns, CJK character takes two — every console table containing CJK text comes ragged. Pad truncate width columns line :
code: labels <- c("中文", "abcd", "日本語")  nchar(labels)      # all look comparable #> [1] 2 4 3 cjk_width(labels)  # they are not #> [1] 4 4 6 cat(paste0("|", cjk_pad(labels, 8), "|"), sep = "\n") #> |中文    | #> |abcd    | #> |日本語  |  cjk_truncate("我今天很開心", 8) #> [1] "我今..."

title: Tidy Tools for Chinese, Japanese and Korean Text
text: usual advice run NFKC. NFKC fix width, also rewrites ligatures, Roman numerals, circled numbers compatibility ideographs. to_halfwidth() changes width nothing else. Halfwidth katakana writes voiced syllable two code points. Composing one difference text matches literal text silently doesn’t:
code: to_halfwidth("１２３")          # fullwidth digits that would not parse #> [1] "123" as.numeric(to_halfwidth("１２３")) #> [1] 123  to_halfwidth("½ Ⅸ ①")          # NFKC would mangle all three; this leaves them #> [1] "½ Ⅸ ①" x <- "ｶﾞ"          # U+FF76 U+FF9E — two code points nchar(x) #> [1] 2 nchar(to_halfwidth(x))          # one: U+30AC #> [1] 1 to_halfwidth(x) == "ガ" #> [1] TRUE
